豚.meaning: Every full <part>moon</part>, the farmer's <part>pig</part> sneaks into the kitchen and reads the menu on the wall. Tonight it says 'roast with apple sauce', and its curly tail goes straight. It runs for the hills: it has no wish to be <kanji>pork</kanji>.
豚.on: The cook chases it round the yard, snapping a pair of kitchen <sound>ton</sound>gs.
豚.kun: The pig hides behind a <sound>bu</sound>lldozer, trembling under a giant <sound>ta</sound>co shell.

強.meaning: An <part>insect</part> no bigger than a grain of rice picks up a huge <part>bow</part>, braces its <part>elbow</part> and pulls the string back until the wood creaks. Twang! The arrow flies clean over the hill. Tiny, but very <kanji>strong</kanji>.
強.on: As the arrow sails off, the insect shouts where it's aimed, '<sound>Kyo</sound>to!', stretching the start as long as the arrow's flight.
強.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' sneezes the insect, then lifts a whole pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt over its head.

張.meaning: An archer ties a <part>long</part> rope to the tip of his <part>bow</part> and pulls it across the yard, tighter and tighter, until it's as tight as a tightrope. Then he hangs out his washing on it. He knows how to <kanji>stretch</kanji> a line.
張.on: His pearl <sound>cho</sound>ker hangs on the line too, swinging in the wind.
張.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' he laughs, as a cat strolls along the stretched rope.

頑.meaning: A <part>rubber duck</part> plants itself on a <part>sawhorse</part> in the middle of the road and won't budge. Cars honk, the mayor pleads, a bulldozer nudges it: nothing. It just stares straight ahead. What a <kanji>stubborn</kanji> duck.
頑.on: Someone has glued it down with a blob of green <sound>gun</sound>k, so it's stuck for good.
頑.kun: They try to bribe it with a <sound>ca</sound>rp, a <sound>ta</sound>co and a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo clock: it won't even blink.

多.meaning: One <part>evening</part> moon rises, then another right on top of it. More pop up behind those, until the sky is crowded with crescents bumping into each other. Two would be a lot, but tonight there are <kanji>many</kanji>.
多.on: The moons tumble into the bath and fill the whole <sound>tu</sound>b.
多.kun: '<sound>Ohh</sound>!' gasps everyone in the street, staring up at all those moons.

対.meaning: On one side of the lawn, a <part>dancer</part> spins and leaps; on the other, a golfer swings a <part>golf club</part>. They glare at each other: whose sport is better? The crowd picks sides and starts to chant. It's dance <kanji>versus</kanji> golf.
対.on: It ends in a draw, a <sound>tie</sound>, so they both get a medal.
対.kun: The dancer keeps one <sound>eye</sound> on the golfer, her <sound>te</sound>nnis opponent tomorrow.
